resenas.frase: An album that consolidates and amplifies both 2023’s debut Dead Meat and last year’s Cotton Crown, transcending notions of what indie rock is supposed to be in the 21st century

It’s a ludicrous, entirely unexpected occurrence when a band release a single album that sounds like a Greatest Hits collection, but track after track, hook after blinding hook, and line after wry line, that’s what we get – every song building on the glistening brilliance of the last
A record that is a ridiculously hook-heavy collection of songs - and one that unquestionably positions Williams as one of our most unique and arresting contemporary songwriters. Print edition only
The band’s post-punk-infused songs sink in quickly and stand up to repeat listens
The Welsh band's classic rock twisted indie folk on their third album demonstrates their earwormy ability to write a hook
Their most fine-tuned and sonically rich album to date, with 12 more fantastically catchy and emotionally turbulent songs in the style they’ve been perfecting along the way
Britain’s best indie-rockers hold fast to their defiantly old-school sound, slipping wry sideways looks at despair in among hooky melodies that always sound like a good time
A consistently impressive record from a singular songwriting talent, brought to life by a remarkably talented band
The UK band’s Merge debut is an album of survival: a set of fatalistic jangle-rock anthems with just enough joy to keep going

On Hard Life, the Tubs finally homed in on a sound to match their self-supplied and tongue-in-cheek “Celtic jangle boyband” tagline. However, the description still fails to capture the London quartet’s complex context and the roughed-up heart that beats in their songs
There’s only so many jangly guitars, high-pitched vocals, and tales of moving to the big smoke that one needs in an album before it starts to grate
